newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post 57th record close of 1996.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post 57th record close of 1996.

text.p: Toronto stocks posted their 57th record close of the year on Thursday, powered by rebounding bank stocks which offset heavy losses in precious metals.
The TSE 300 Composite Index shrugged off early weakness to close up 21.90 points at 5820.91. The key index also set an intraday peak of 5824.92.
Trading was brisk with 115 million shares worth C$1.9 billion ($1.4 billion) changing hands.
"Gold was down, but the financial services sector is pretty attractive right now," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities.
Toronto's bank group -- which has hit all-time highs this autumn -- fell sharply earlier this week due to profit-taking.
Several bank stocks were among the TSE's top gainers as the financial services group added 120 points.

The market's eight strong sectors also included communications, conglomerates and energy issues. Those gains were restrained by a 198-point loss in precious metals as gold prices snapped a five-day rally to finish lower on Thursday.

Analysts said investors were encouraged by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen's comment on interest rates earlier today. Thiessen told reporters that Canada's economic fundamentals suggest the country's current low rates are sustainable.
"These (economic) fundamentals have led to growing confidence among both Canadian and foreign investors that the lower interest rates can be sustained," he said.

* Southam Inc. closed up 0.45 at 19 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 19.25. Hollinger Inc. raised its offer for seven million Southam shares to C$20 ($15) per share from C$18.75 ($14) late Wednesday.
* Sears Canada Inc. finished up 0.45 at 11.65 after reaching a 52-week peak of 12 on 1.9 million shares. Analysts said the retailer has slashed costs and sharply reduced its losses in recent months.
* Among the banks, Toronto-Dominion Bank rose 1.25 to 33.90, while Bank of Nova Scotia gained 1.40 to 45.30.
* Weak gold stocks topped the TSE's most-active list. Kinross Gold Corp. fell 0.70 to 10.05 on 3.5 million shares, while Barrick Gold Corp. dropped 0.30 to 37.70 on 3.3 million shares.
* Thomson Corp. jumped 0.95 to 27.50 on 2.3 million shares. The company reported higher nine-month profits due to stronger core earnings and higher net gains from asset sales.
